backlog.title: Distributed-PRD Include Dedup Polish (PRD §2.3 bugfixes)
backlog.description: Apply three rigorously-validated MINOR fixes (PRD §2.3 / Minor Issues) to the distributed (multi-file) PRD include resolver in src/core/session-utils.ts and src/config/constants.ts. The core include-dedup contract is already sound and fully tested (67-test suite passes): global-flat dedup, elision, idempotency as a fixed point, and exponential-blowup protection are all verified. These three issues are (1) stale user-facing JSDoc for the collision-proof @! marker format (BUG-001), (2) a missing stderr warning for a stale .md token at the maxDepth depth-gate (BUG-002), and (3) the dedup visited set keying on a lexical path instead of the canonical realpath so symlink aliases to one physical file fail to dedup (BUG-003). No new features, no behavioral surface added beyond closing these three gaps. Research findings are persisted in plan/014_347986b2effd/bugfix/002_2b460dab1a1f/architecture/ (system_context.md, bugfix_findings.md, external_deps.md).

milestones.title: Resolve the three validated minor defects and sync docs
milestones.description: Fix BUG-001 (JSDoc drift), BUG-002 (depth-gate stale .md warning), and BUG-003 (symlink-safe canonical dedup key), then run a final changeset-level doc sweep. The three implementation tasks are independent (disjoint source regions: BUG-001 is constants.ts only; BUG-002 edits neutralizeResolvableTokens + the resolvePRD stale-warning JSDoc bullet; BUG-003 edits expandIncludesRecursive visited keying + the entry pre-seed + the resolvePRD dedup JSDoc bullet). They MAY run in parallel; if serialized, any order is valid. The final doc-sweep task depends on all three implementation subtasks and runs last. Definition of Done for each: failing test first (where behavior changes), implementation, passing test, typecheck (`npm run typecheck`), lint (`npm run lint`), and `npm run test:run` green for the touched suites.

tasks.title: BUG-001: Update stale PRD_INCLUDE_MARKERS JSDoc to match the emitted collision-proof @! markers
tasks.description: The PRD_INCLUDE_MARKERS env-var JSDoc in src/config/constants.ts documents the OLD marker format (<!-- @include: path --> / <!-- @end-include -->) while the resolver actually emits the collision-proof <!-- @!include: path --> / <!-- @!end-include --> and elision <!-- @!include-ref: path -->. DECISION (recorded in bugfix_findings.md): KEEP the @! format (it is correct, structurally non-resolvable, and already locked by the BUG-001 collision test). The defect is purely doc drift. Fix the JSDoc only; do NOT change emitted markers or add behavior.

subtasks.title: Rewrite the stale PRD_INCLUDE_MARKERS JSDoc in constants.ts to document the actual @!include / @!end-include / @!include-ref markers

CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/014_347986b2effd/bugfix/002_2b460dab1a1f/architecture/bugfix_findings.md §BUG-001 and system_context.md. The emitted format is locked by tests/unit/core/prd-markers.test.ts (the 'BUG-001: markers are STRUCTURALLY non-resolvable' test + the 'wraps expanded includes when PRD_INCLUDE_MARKERS is set' test). docs/CONFIGURATION.md:310 and README.md:135 ALREADY use the correct @!include format — this subtask touches ONLY src/config/constants.ts.
2. INPUT: The exact stale block is src/config/constants.ts JSDoc on `export const PRD_INCLUDE_MARKERS` (around lines 1282-1300): summary line `* Environment variable name: emit <!-- @include --> markers around expanded includes` and `@remarks` `When set, resolved include output emits <!-- @include: path --> / <!-- @end-include --> comment markers, and a .md token that fails to resolve (stale include) emits a stderr warning.`
3. LOGIC: Rewrite ONLY this JSDoc block to document the ACTUALLY-EMITTED markers: open `<!-- @!include: path -->`, close `<!-- @!end-include -->`, and elided-2nd-reference `<!-- @!include-ref: path -->`. Add ONE sentence explaining the collision-proof rationale (the `!` after `@` is outside the RESOLVE_TOKEN char-class `[A-Za-z0-9_./-]`, so the markers are structurally non-resolvable → a true idempotent fixed point even when files named include/end-include/include-ref exist). KEEP the existing clause that a stale `.md` token emits a stderr warning. Keep the `@example` block and the `export const PRD_INCLUDE_MARKERS = 'PRD_INCLUDE_MARKERS';` declaration UNCHANGED. Do NOT touch expandIncludesRecursive / elisionRefComment emission. Do NOT alter docs/CONFIGURATION.md or README.md here (those are verified in the Mode-B sweep task P1.M1.T4).
4. OUTPUT: constants.ts JSDoc that matches emitted markers; no code/behavior change. Verified by `npm run typecheck`, `npm run docs:check`, and the existing prd-markers.test.ts suite still passing (`npm run test:run -- prd-markers`).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] This subtask IS the doc fix for the constants.ts JSDoc it touches — no separate docs subtask for this file. Cross-cutting overview docs (README/CONFIGURATION/ARCHITECTURE/CLI_REFERENCE) are handled by the Mode-B final task P1.M1.T4.
6. TEST: No new test (doc-only JSDoc; behavior already locked by the existing BUG-001 collision test). Confirm the marker tests still pass.

tasks.title: BUG-002: Emit exactly one stderr warning for a stale .md token at the maxDepth depth-gate
tasks.description: neutralizeResolvableTokens (called when depth >= maxDepth) leaves a non-resolvable .md token verbatim and, by design, emits NO stale-include warning — violating the unconditional PRD §2.3 MUST ('A .md token that fails to resolve (stale include) MUST emit a stderr warning'). Route stale .md detection through the gate so a deeply-nested typo'd include still warns. Output idempotency is unaffected (warn is side-effect only; the token still survives verbatim).

subtasks.title: Add the stale-.md stderr warning to neutralizeResolvableTokens and correct the two now-wrong JSDoc spots
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/014_347986b2effd/bugfix/002_2b460dab1a1f/architecture/bugfix_findings.md §BUG-002 and system_context.md. The working stale-warning lives in expandIncludesRecursive (`console.warn(`[prd-resolver] stale include '@${token}': path does not resolve to an existing file (${abs})`)`, routed via console.warn → process.stderr because the pino logger writes stdout). The depth gate is neutralizeResolvableTokens(content, baseDir, markers) in src/core/session-utils.ts, called early in expandIncludesRecursive when `depth >= maxDepth`.
2. INPUT: neutralizeResolvableTokens already computes `token`, `abs = resolve(baseDir, token)`, and a boolean `resolves` (true iff an existing FILE). Its non-resolving branch currently emits `out += m[0]` (verbatim) and nothing else. Its JSDoc says 'Emits NO stale-include warning (elision = success; verbatim = non-resolving prose, which is silent).'
3. LOGIC: In the non-resolving branch, when `!resolves && token.endsWith('.md')`, emit EXACTLY ONE `console.warn` with the SAME message format as the main loop: `console.warn(`[prd-resolver] stale include '@${token}': path does not resolve to an existing file (${abs})`)`. Do NOT warn for elided (resolvable) tokens, non-`.md` tokens, or successfully-resolved tokens — only `!resolves && token.endsWith('.md')`. Keep emitting `out += m[0]` (token stays verbatim). Verify the maxDepth=0 edge (gate fires at entry) correctly warns for a stale .md in the entry — this is spec-correct per the unconditional MUST. No double-warn risk: a gate token only ever passes through neutralizeResolvableTokens (the gate returns early), never the main loop.
4. OUTPUT: A stale `.md` token at any depth (including the gate) emits exactly one stderr warning per resolve pass; output bytes are UNCHANGED (idempotency preserved — re-resolution re-warns once per pass, which is spec-correct and does not alter output). Consumed by callers that observe stderr (no interface change).
5. DOCS: [Mode A] (a) Rewrite the neutralizeResolvableTokens JSDoc line 'Emits NO stale-include warning …' to: a non-resolvable `.md` token (ENOENT or directory) at the gate emits exactly one stderr warning (PRD §2.3 MUST); elided tokens, non-`.md` survivors, and resolved tokens are silent. (b) In the resolvePRD `@remarks` STALE-INCLUDE WARNING bullet, the current list says 'depth-exceeded tokens … emit NO warning' — reword so a STALE `.md` at the depth gate is NOT listed as silent (it now warns once per pass), while elided/cycle/diamond tokens and successfully-resolved tokens remain correctly listed as silent.
6. TEST: Write the failing test FIRST in tests/unit/core/prd-markers.test.ts (within the existing 'resolvePRD — markers, stale warnings, idempotency' describe style, REAL tmpdir, `vi.spyOn(console,'warn').mockImplementation(() => {})`): (a) g.md='G @missing.md END', main.md='@g.md', resolvePRD(main,{maxDepth:1}) → warn called exactly 1×, call[0] contains 'missing.md', output === 'G @missing.md END'. (b) Negative: g.md='G @missing.txt END' at gate → warn NOT called. (c) Negative: g.md references a real h.md at maxDepth=1 → warn NOT called and @h.md is elided (not literal). Then implement to pass. Run `npm run test:run -- prd-markers prd-resolve`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`.

tasks.title: BUG-003: Key the dedup visited set on the canonical realpath so symlink aliases dedup
tasks.description: The global-flat dedup visited set keys on the lexical path.resolve result at three sites (elision `has` check, mark-visited `add`, and the entry pre-seed in resolvePRD). Two symlinks to one physical file get distinct keys and the file is expanded twice, defeating dedup. Switch the KEY (and only the key) to the realpath-resolved canonical path with a safe lexical fallback, applied uniformly at all three sites.

subtasks.title: Introduce a canonical dedupKey(realpathSync with lexical fallback) and apply it to all three visited-set sites + entry pre-seed
subtasks.context_scope:
CONTRACT DEFINITION:
1. RESEARCH NOTE: See plan/014_347986b2effd/bugfix/002_2b460dab1a1f/architecture/bugfix_findings.md §BUG-003 and system_context.md. realpathSync is NOT yet imported (stat is from node:fs/promises, line 33-34; node:path resolve/join/dirname/basename imported line 35). The THREE keying sites are: (a) elision check `if (visited.has(abs))` where abs=resolve(baseDir,token) in expandIncludesRecursive (~line 516); (b) mark-visited `visited.add(abs)` after st.isFile() (~line 525); (c) entry pre-seed `new Set<string>([absEntry])` in resolvePRD (~line 716), where absEntry=resolve(prdPath). On macOS the tmpdir is symlinked (/var/folders → /private/var/folders), so ALL THREE sites MUST use the SAME canonical key or self-include/entry-back-edge elision tests break.
2. INPUT: The `visited: Set<string>` shared global-flat set and the existing `abs`/`absEntry` lexical values. No interface/signature change to expandIncludesRecursive or resolvePRD.
3. LOGIC: (1) Add `import { realpathSync } from 'node:fs';`. (2) Add a private helper near expandIncludesRecursive: `function dedupKey(abs: string): string { try { return realpathSync(abs); } catch { return abs; } }` with a doc comment noting the fallback is for non-resolvable paths (realpathSync throws on ENOENT; visited.add only runs for existing files and the entry pre-seed is an existing file, so the fallback mainly guards the elision `has` check for not-yet-stat'd/stale tokens, which are never in visited anyway). Add a code comment noting the one-sync-syscall-per-encounter cost is acceptable (dedup bounds encounters to one per file; PRDs are small). (3) Replace the key at all three sites: `if (visited.has(dedupKey(abs)))`, `visited.add(dedupKey(abs))`, and `new Set<string>([dedupKey(absEntry)])`. Do NOT change marker tokens, message output, or stat semantics — ONLY the visited key.
4. OUTPUT: Two symlink aliases to one physical file dedup correctly (second reference elided). Existing real-file dedup tests (diamond/cycle/self-include/entry-back-edge) keep passing: for non-symlink files realpathSync(abs) === normalized abs and behavior (content appears once) is unchanged; tests assert dedup BEHAVIOR, not the key string.
5. DOCS: [Mode A] (a) Update the expandIncludesRecursive `@param visited` doc to state the key is the canonical (realpath-resolved) absolute path (symlink-safe). (b) In resolvePRD `@remarks` GLOBAL-FLAT-DEDUP bullet, change 'keyed on the resolved absolute path' → 'keyed on the canonical (realpath-resolved) absolute path, so symlink aliases to the same physical file dedup correctly'. Keep all other dedup/elision wording.
6. TEST: Write the failing test FIRST in tests/unit/core/prd-resolve.test.ts (REAL tmpdir; add symlinkSync to the node:fs import): real.md='REAL'; symlinkSync(join(tmp,'real.md'), join(tmp,'alias.md')); main.md='@real.md @alias.md'; resolvePRD(main) → output === 'REAL ' and out.split('REAL').length === 2 (appears exactly once). If a symlink-capability guard is added, document why (primary dev platform supports symlinkSync). Then implement to pass. Run `npm run test:run -- prd-resolve prd-markers`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`.
